Without sounding like a fan boy, I would like some advice

I prefer different brands for different reasons. Glock as a throwaway since I get LE discounts and all that, so its cheap and don't care if it gets broke or something. Use 1911 style for competition. And carry a Sig.

My friend will pretty much only buy Sig.

Everyone is different, so its up to you. I was accurate with the 9mm PX4 and enjoyed shooting it. However I don't think I'd enjoy shooting it as a 45. I leave 45 to the heavy larger guns. That's just me though. I'd have a 1911 in 45, 9, and 22 if I could. So call it redundant, who cares? I think it's great to have a gun for carry and a gun in the house for defense. So its a bonus they are the same platform.

It's also past 1am so I'll come back tomorrow and see if what I said made any sense.

Handguns are very personal things. The weight and shape and balance needs to fit your hands so that it points naturally, and so that it invites a constant grip from time to time and from shot to shot.

The sights have to be friendly to your eyes. The action type has to work well with your habits and expectations. It needs to inspire confidence and it helps if it inspires affection.

Self-defense applications are the most important of all. If it literally comes down to fighting for your life one day, there's the very best gun for you, and there's the ones that aren't. There's nothing in between.

If you have something that works well for you, stick with it. Maybe someday you'll find something new that works better, and you can change your habits then.
